primary_modality_specific: Subcutaneous cyclic hexapeptide intrahelical orthosteric Site-2 C5aR1 complement receptor antagonist (PMX 205 / ALS-205, CID:6918845)

primary_modality_specific: High-dose CNS-penetrant N-acetylcysteine regimen (>=50-70 mg/kg/d parenteral or high-dose oral; distinct from low-dose <=600 mg/d oral NAC)
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Bye 2025 Rank #12/107 (+0.9458d, p=0.0201, q_BH=0.0936, n=15) did not survive BH-FDR and may reflect extracellular thiol media buffering, YET neither clinical futility nor insurmountable CNS PK deficit is established: Louwerse et al. 1995 PMID:7763202 (50 mg/kg/d SC NAC [~3,500 mg/d at 70 kg], N=110) was an underpowered trial whose survival CI includes substantial benefit alongside opposing onset strata (overall HR=0.74 [95% CI 0.41-1.33], p=0.31; limb-onset n=81 HR=0.50 [0.24-1.04], p=0.06 vs bulbar-onset n=29 HR=1.66 [0.56-4.99]), and Katz et al. 2015 PMID:25765302 demonstrated in N=12 Parkinson participants over 2 days (LP 90 min post-dose) that 70 mg/kg oral NAC BID achieves 9.26 +/- 1.62 uM human CSF NAC (p<0.001) without acute DLT, whereas recruiting NCT07414212 (N=90) administers 600 mg/d oral effervescent NAC (5.83x lower nominal daily mass than 3,500 mg/d SC across ~6-10% oral bioavailability; cf. lipophilic NACA/AD4 prodrugs and ALSUntangled #82 review PMID:41777232) co-formulated with 1,800 mg/d EH301 (1,500 mg nicotinamide riboside + 300 mg pterostilbene) + 100 mg riluzole, precluding single-agent NAC attribution.
discriminating_next_test: Separate extracellular thiol media-oxidation buffering (using Catalase/GSH-ethyl-ester/GCLC-inhibition controls) from intracellular neuronal glutathione rescue in human sALS iPSC-MNs, and require paired human ALS CSF free-NAC and 7T/3T MRS cortical/cervical GSH target-engagement proof at high-dose (>=50-70 mg/kg) dosing before efficacy testing.

primary_modality_specific: High-dose oral L-serine amino-acid supplementation (15 g BID = 30 g/d) with proposed prospective SPTLC1/SPTLC2 genetic & sphingolipid screening
key_quantitative_anchor: [MEASURED] Bye 2025 2.5 uM survival delta (+0.7117d, Rank #20/107, nominal p=0.04190, q_BH=0.17067 across 16 sALS lines) reflects a fixed-library-concentration endpoint mismatch where adding 2.5 uM increases ~400 uM basal BrainPhys/DMEM-F12 media L-serine concentration by only +0.625% (leaving clinical 15 g BID = 30 g/d systemic exposure untested in physiological low-serine media without proving clinical underdosing); zero concurrent-placebo-controlled sALS efficacy trials have completed (Phase 1 NCT01835782 N=20 Levine et al. 2017 PMID:27589995 — motivated historically by Cox/Dunlop cyanobacterial BMAA seryl-tRNA misincorporation alongside HSAN1 SPT 1-deoxysphingolipid suppression — was randomized and double-blind across 4 dose levels [0.5, 2.5, 7.5, 15 g BID] compared against matched historical placebo controls with no concurrent placebo arm; single-arm Phase 2 NCT03580616 N=43 terminated for IRB noncompliance), while human ALS genetics motivates a proposed genetic/lipid safeguard: rare ALS-linked SPTLC1/SPTLC2 GoF variants (sporadic prevalence rare and cohort-dependent) disrupt ORMDL ceramide feedback and overproduce canonical C18-C22 dihydrosphingolipids/ceramides (variant-specific biochemical risk distinct from HSAN1 1-deoxysphingolipid variants; Mohassel et al. 2021 PMID:34059824; Ziak et al. 2026 PMID:43025655, 10.1016/j.jlr.2026.101187; targeted by intrathecal SPTLC1 ASO LTX-002 NCT07660614).
discriminating_next_test: Quantify 1-deoxysphingolipid vs canonical C18-C22 ceramide flux and dose-response survival across physiological CSF-like low-serine (~25-40 uM) human sALS iPSC-MN media (0-1,000 uM L-serine), and incorporate prospective SPTLC1/SPTLC2 sequencing + plasma sphingolipid profiling as a safety safeguard before any concurrent-placebo-controlled sporadic ALS trial.

C9orf72 PMID:27723745 — opposite phospho-sign to dephospho-cofilin rods) observed elevated pSer3-CFL1 in postmortem human sALS spinal MNs and demonstrated in experimental cellular/model perturbations that LIMK1-driven Ser3 hyperphosphorylation (inactivation) promotes TDP-43 aggregation, whereas direct CFL1 inhibition is barred by pan-essentiality (DepMap p10 Chronos=-1.3534; gnomAD v4.1 MANE ENST00000308162 LOEUF=0.408, pLI=0.990, mis_z=3.38) and upstream ROCK1/2 blockade (Fasudil, which de-represses CFL1) showed no clinical separation in 20-d Phase 2a ROCK-ALS (NCT03792490, N=120, PMID:39424560) or Bye 2025 (p=0.209).
